topics.name: Degrees of comparison (as ... as, No other ...)
Modals for permission and advice (may, shall, had better)
Do as directed: assertive and word forms

options: The Emperors court was full of scholars.
The Emperor's court was full of scholars.
The Emperor's court were full of scholars.
questions.rule: The court belongs to the Emperor: Emperor's. One court takes was.

options: May I have your permission to speak?
May I having your permission to speak?
May I has your permission to speak?
questions.rule: After a modal like may, use the base form of the verb: have.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: than needs the comparative degree: wittier than.
as + plain adjective + as: as clever as a fox.

questions.before: Pundit Shahane had never heard of the scripture,
questions.rule: so joins a cause to its result. 'Because of' and 'due to' need a noun, not a clause.
Commands are reported with told/ordered + person + to + verb.

chat: May I announce the guest now, Your Majesty?
options: Yes, you may announce him now.
Yes, you may announces him now.
Yes, you mays announce him now.
questions.rule: A modal never takes -s, and the verb after it stays in the base form: may announce.

options: She asked me if was I hungry.
She asked me if I was hungry.
She asked me that was I hungry.
questions.rule: A reported yes/no question uses if + statement order: if I was hungry.

options: Riya asked what the score was.
Riya asked what was the score.
Riya asked that what the score was.
questions.rule: Use asked, no 'that' before the wh-word, statement order (the score was), and move the tense back: was.

questions.source: Tenali Raman was wittier than Pundit Shahane.
options: Pundit Shahane was as witty as Tenali Raman.
Pundit Shahane was not as witty as Tenali Raman.
Pundit Shahane was not as wittier as Tenali Raman.
questions.rule: Swap the two and use not as + plain adjective + as.

options: The coach ordered the players run faster.
The coach ordered the players that run faster.
The coach ordered the players to run faster.
questions.rule: Reported command: ordered + person + to + verb.

options: Raman was clever, so he win the debate.
Raman was clever, so he won the debate.
Raman was clever, so won he the debate.
questions.rule: After so use normal order and keep the past tense: he won.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: had better is followed by the base form: had better leave.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With a past reporting verb the tense moves back: am becomes was.
A reported yes/no question is joined with if (or whether).

questions.before: No other scholar in the court was as
questions.rule: No other ... as + plain adjective + as.
Offers use Shall I + base verb?

chat: Why didn't you come to the cricket match?
options: I had a fever, so I stay at home.
I had a fever, so I stayed at home.
I had a fever, so I staying at home.
questions.rule: Both clauses are about the past: had ... stayed.

questions.source: Raman was rewarded. He saved the honour of the empire.
options: Raman was rewarded because he saved the honour of the empire.
Raman was rewarded because he saves the honour of the empire.
Raman was rewarded because of he saved the honour of the empire.
questions.rule: because + a full clause; keep the past tense: he saved.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: told us to + base verb: to bring. After a modal: should practise.

options: Mother exclaimed with delight that how beautiful the garden looked.
Mother exclaimed with delight that the garden looked very beautifully.
Mother exclaimed with delight that the garden looked very beautiful.
questions.rule: In a reported exclamation, 'how' becomes very, the tense moves back (looked), and after 'looked' we use an adjective.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: one of the most ... is followed by a plural noun: scholars.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After the past verb asked, the reported question moves back: what he wanted.

questions.after: better be quiet during the debate.
questions.rule: The fixed phrase for strong advice is had better + base verb.
In a reported question the subject comes before the verb: where I had kept.

chat: What did the principal say in the assembly?
options: She told us not to run in the corridors.
She told us to not running in the corridors.
She told us don't run in the corridors.
questions.rule: A negative command is reported with told + person + not to + verb.

chat: Who is the best player in your team?
options: Rohan is the best of all.
Rohan is the most best of all.
Rohan is best than all of us.
questions.rule: best is already superlative: the best. Never 'most best' or 'best than'.

questions.source: How can anyone forget such a clever trick?
options: Anyone can forget such a clever trick.
No one can forgets such a clever trick.
No one can forget such a clever trick.
questions.rule: A question that expects 'no' becomes a negative statement: No one can forget.

questions.source: The Emperor said to the guards, "Bring Tenali Raman at once."
options: The Emperor ordered the guards that bring Tenali Raman at once.
The Emperor ordered the guards to bring Tenali Raman at once.
The Emperor ordered the guards to brought Tenali Raman at once.
questions.rule: Reported command: ordered + person + to + base verb.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: not as wise as uses the plain adjective; the story is past, so he conceded.

options: Raman said that he had bring the scripture with him.
Raman said that he had brought the scripture with him.
Raman said that he have brought the scripture with him.
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had brought.

options: Pundit Shahanes visit to our court was an open challenge.
Pundit Shahane's visit to our court was an open challenge.
Pundit Shahane's visit to our court were an open challenge.
questions.rule: The visit belongs to Pundit Shahane, so add 's: Shahane's visit. One visit takes was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The reason clause is in the past perfect, so the result is in the simple past: he gave up.

questions.after: of the scripture that Raman mentioned.
questions.rule: was unaware of + noun means 'did not know about'.

questions.before: Pundit Shahane asked the courtiers what
questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order with no 'did/does': what the name meant.
No other + noun + comparative + than.

chat: Can I borrow your costume for the skit?
options: Of course you could, but please returning it by Friday.
Of course you can, but please returns it by Friday.
Of course you can, but please return it by Friday.
questions.rule: A request with please uses the base verb: please return.

questions.source: Grandpa said to me, "Have you finished your homework?"
options: Grandpa asked me if had I finished my homework.
Grandpa asked me if I had finished my homework.
Grandpa asked me that had I finished my homework.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked + if (not 'that'), statement order, and present perfect becomes had finished.

questions.source: Raman was the wittiest poet in the court.
options: No other poet in the court was as witty as Raman.
No other poet in the court was as wittiest as Raman.
No other poet in the court were as witty as Raman.
questions.rule: Superlative becomes No other ... was as + plain adjective + as.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Passive: will be held; yesterday needs the past: asked; told me to learn.

options: The Emperor asked Raman to what great work had he referred.
The Emperor asked Raman to what great work he had refer.
The Emperor asked Raman to what great work he had referred.
questions.rule: A reported question takes statement order, and the past moves back: he had referred (had + past participle).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The main verb of this past story needs the simple past: Raman ... thanked the Emperor.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Comparing one with all the others (more than two) needs the superlative: the most confident.

questions.before: The Emperor exclaimed with joy that it
questions.rule: After the past verb exclaimed, the tense moves back, and 'it' is singular: it was.
Reported wh-question: asked + person + wh-word + subject + verb, no 'did'.

chat: What did Pundit Shahane say before he left?
options: He said that he had not read that scripture.
He said that he not had read that scripture.
He said to he had not read that scripture.
questions.rule: Reported statement: said that + past perfect, with 'not' after 'had'.

options: I think Raman is as cleverer as Birbal.
I think Raman is so clever than Birbal.
I think Raman is as clever as Birbal.
questions.rule: Equal comparison: as + plain adjective + as.

questions.prompt: Rewrite using the noun form of 'proud'.
questions.rule: The noun of proud is pride, and we say take pride in.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Keep the story in the past: dared, suggested; asked everyone to honour (to + base verb).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Clauses joined by when and and keep the same past tense: opened, laughed, praised.
